title: Haaland Scores Twice. Neymar Says Goodbye. Norway End Brazil's World Cup Dream at MetLife.
excerpt: The Manchester City striker headed in the opener and fired an unstoppable second as Norway reached the quarterfinals for the first time. Brazil haven't made the last eight since 1990.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Norway reached the World Cup quarterfinals for the first time, defeating Brazil 2-1.
  • Erling Haaland scored both goals for Norway, showcasing his striking prowess.
  • Neymar confirmed his retirement from the Brazilian national team after the match.
  • Brazil has not reached the World Cup quarterfinals since 2018, marking a significant decline.
  • Haaland is now tied for the Golden Boot with seven tournament goals.
Norway's Historic Victory
›Norway's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance.
›Erling Haaland scored twice in 11 minutes.
›Brazil eliminated before quarterfinals for second consecutive tournament.
›Match held at MetLife Stadium with 80,000 attendees.
Sources: Reuters, Fox Sports

For 79 minutes at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, a city where Indian restaurants line Oak Tree Road and NRI families packed the stands wearing every jersey imaginable, the scoreboard read 0-0. Brazil had dominated possession. Norway had survived a penalty scare. And Erling Haaland, the tournament's most feared striker, had barely touched the ball.

Then, in the span of eleven minutes, he reminded 80,000 people — and a few hundred million more watching at home — why he is called The Terminator.

The Header That Changed Everything

Norway coach Ståle Solbakken made a halftime gamble, replacing both wingers and sending on Andreas Schjelderup and Oscar Bobb. It was a masterstroke. Schjelderup swung in a cross from the left flank in the 79th minute, and Haaland — a full head above every Brazilian defender — powered a header into the bottom corner.

"It felt like a gift from God that it actually went into the net," Haaland said afterward, grinning beneath the MetLife floodlights.

Eleven minutes later, Schjelderup found him again. This time Haaland received the ball outside the box, turned, and lasered a low shot between Danilo's legs. The Norwegian bench erupted. The Brazilian one went silent.

![Andreas Schjelderup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1c/Andreas_Schjelderup_Morocco_v_Norway_7_June_2026-43_%28cropped%29.jpg)

> **"This is one of the most insane days in Norwegian history."

Norway, a country of 5.5 million people that has never reached a World Cup quarterfinal before, will now face England in Miami on Saturday."**

Neymar's Last Dance

Brazil's agony deepened in stoppage time when Neymar, 34, converted a late penalty to make it 2-1 — a consolation that changed only the scoreline. After the final whistle, the man who once carried an entire nation's hopes on his shoulders confirmed what many suspected: this was his last game in the *Seleção* jersey.

It was a fitting, if painful, bookend. Neymar came on as a substitute for Gabriel Martinelli in the 68th minute, was booked for dissent, and then scored the goal that kept Brazil's dignity intact. But it wasn't enough.

The Penalty That Wasn't

The match could have gone differently. In the 13th minute, Norway centre-back Kristoffer Ajer clumsily brought down Matheus Cunha in the box. Penalty. But instead of Vinícius Júnior stepping up — the man who has scored from the spot all season for Real Madrid — it was Bruno Guimarães who took the kick.

Ørjan Nyland dived left and saved it. The MetLife crowd, heavily Brazilian, fell silent. Guimarães stood frozen. Carlo Ancelotti, the legendary manager who has won everything in club football, sat stone-faced in the dugout.

![Oscar Bobb — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/54/ManCity20240722-050_%28Oscar_Bobb2%29.jpg)

Neymar's Farewell
›Neymar scored a late penalty for Brazil.
›Confirmed retirement from the national team post-match.
›Came on as a substitute in the 68th minute.
›Was booked for dissent during the match.
Sources: Reuters, Fox Sports

Brazil have not reached the World Cup quarterfinals since 2018 and have now been eliminated before the last eight for the second consecutive tournament. For a country that has won the trophy five times, this is a crisis.

Haaland Joins the Golden Boot Race

With seven goals in the tournament, Haaland now sits level with Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappé in the race for the Golden Boot. He has scored in 14 consecutive competitive internationals — a record that would make most strikers' entire careers.

"Maybe this will write history in Norway," he said. "Everyone just needs to enjoy themselves. This is one of the most insane days in Norwegian history."

Norway, a country of 5.5 million people that has never reached a World Cup quarterfinal before, will now face England in Miami on Saturday. England survived their own ordeal at the Azteca Stadium, beating co-hosts Mexico 3-2 with ten men after Jude Bellingham's stunning brace and Harry Kane's captain's penalty.

What It Means for NRIs in the Stands

For the tens of thousands of Indian-origin fans who watched the match live at MetLife — located in the heart of New Jersey's massive Indian diaspora corridor — it was a tournament-defining afternoon. Many had bought tickets hoping to see Neymar and Vinícius Júnior put on a show. Instead, they witnessed something rarer: the fall of a giant and the rise of a Viking.
